inheritedStart: Run the RC48-proposed counter-bound Merkle fault test on 10,000 synthetic events; do not fit another X16 image model and do not use an unavailable historical sidecar.
question: Which combination of event identity and boundary integrity can distinguish omission, duplication, reordering, counter-domain reset, and payload mutation at capture, export, and packaging, and which faults remain impossible to identify because they occur before the first independent commitment?

capabilityAuditBeforeSeal.node: Node.js v25.8.2 provides SHA-256 and Ed25519 in node:crypto.
capabilityAuditBeforeSeal.python: Python cryptography 41.0.3 provides an independent Ed25519 verifier.
capabilityAuditBeforeSeal.boundary: Only module availability and existing repository assets were inspected. No RC49 corpus, fault output, primary verdict, independent verdict, or aggregate metric existed before this file.

corpus.payloadGeneration: SHA-256 over the fixed UTF-8 test label, uint64 event ordinal, and a fixed public corpus salt. Payload bytes are opaque to arm adjudicators and the physical ordinal is not encoded as text.
corpus.trials: Five clean controls plus one trial for every stage × fault × placement combination: 5 + 3×5×5 = 80 trials.
corpus.armEvaluations: counter-only, signature-only, and counter-plus-Merkle each evaluate 80 trials; clock-only reports both tight and loose envelopes for each trial, for 400 arm/regime evaluations total.

faultSemantics.omission: Remove the record generated by the target trigger at the named stage.
faultSemantics.duplicate: Insert a second exact copy of the target record immediately after it at the named stage.
faultSemantics.adjacent-reorder: Swap the target record with its next record at the named stage.
faultSemantics.unannounced-counter-reset: From the target record onward, reset the numerical counter to zero without changing the signed identity-domain name or providing a domain bridge.
faultSemantics.payload-mutation: Flip bit 0 of payload byte 0 on the target record at the named stage while leaving identity fields unchanged.
faultSemantics.stageApplication: A fault injected at capture is present before the capture commitment. Export and package faults occur after the preceding boundary commitment and before the named boundary commitment.

arms.evidence: Final-package records carry identityDomain and uint64 triggerCounter; no intermediate commitment, payload digest, or authenticated stage snapshot is available.
arms.canTest: Event-sequence gaps, duplicates, adjacent inversions, and unannounced reset in the released sequence.
arms.cannotClaim: Cause stage, payload integrity, signature provenance, or correctness of the counter before release.

arms.evidence: Each stage retains an Ed25519-signed RFC9162_SHA256 Merkle root and an ordered anonymous record-token manifest, chained to the previous boundary; counter and clock fields are excluded.
arms.canTest: Stage-to-stage byte-set changes and anonymous record positions after the capture commitment.
arms.cannotClaim: Which physical trigger produced an anonymous token or whether capture input was already wrong before the first root.

arms.evidence: Final records carry one clockDomain and a timestamp center. The tight total error half-width is 40 microseconds; the loose half-width is 60 microseconds; no stage commitment is available.
arms.canTest: A clock identity is robust only when its entire possible-time interval lies inside one 100-microsecond trigger Voronoi cell.
arms.cannotClaim: Stage attribution, payload integrity, or identity after clock reset without a signed domain bridge.

arms.evidence: Every leaf binds version, identityDomain, uint64 triggerCounter, and SHA-256 payload digest using fixed length-prefixed binary encoding. Capture, export, and package roots use RFC 9162 SHA-256 leaf/node domain separation and each Ed25519-signed boundary statement binds stage, tree size, root, previous root, fixture ID, and schema version.
arms.canTest: Physical event identity plus exact boundary localization for structural faults and post-capture byte mutation.
arms.cannotClaim: Payload correctness before the capture commitment, reference-trigger completeness, real key custody, trusted external time, or production-device behavior.

cryptographicProfile.merkle: RFC 9162 MTH: empty HASH(), leaf HASH(0x00 || entry), node HASH(0x01 || left || right), largest-power-of-two split for non-power-of-two trees.
cryptographicProfile.leafEncoding: ASCII domain tag UP-RC49-LEAF-v1 followed by uint32 big-endian byte lengths and UTF-8/binary values; all counters and sizes are uint64 big-endian. No implicit JSON serialization is inside a leaf.
cryptographicProfile.boundaryEncoding: RFC 8785-compatible canonical JSON restricted to strings, booleans, arrays, safe integers, and unique object keys.
cryptographicProfile.signature: Ed25519 with a fixed public synthetic-test seed committed in the implementation. The private seed is intentionally public and provides reproducibility, not operational key security.
cryptographicProfile.manifestRetention: The experiment retains stage leaf inputs for localization. A production design may distribute inclusion proofs instead; RC49 does not claim COSE or SCITT conformance.

competingHypotheses.claim: A counter-bound signed Merkle pipeline identifies every injected fault, including payload corruption before its first commitment.
competingHypotheses.prediction: All 75 fault trials receive exact event-and-stage localization.
competingHypotheses.reject: Reject if a capture-mutated payload is internally consistent with the first signed root; correct behavior is an explicit outside-observable-boundary result.

competingHypotheses.claim: Counters and chained boundary commitments jointly identify all structural faults and all post-capture payload mutations while refusing resets and pre-commit corruption.
competingHypotheses.prediction: Exactly 55 observable faults localize to event and stage, 15 reset trials refuse downstream identity, five capture mutations abstain as pre-commit, and five clean controls remain clean.
competingHypotheses.decisiveTest: All 80 counter-plus-Merkle trials, independently regenerated and adjudicated.
competingHypotheses.reject: Reject on any wrong event, wrong stage, false clean call, accepted reset continuation, invalid signature/root accepted, or disagreement between implementations.

competingHypotheses.claim: Signed Merkle manifests without counters are sufficient to recover physical trigger identities.
competingHypotheses.prediction: Signature-only gives the same exact event-and-stage verdicts as counter-plus-Merkle.
competingHypotheses.decisiveTest: Capture omissions and every post-capture changed anonymous token.
competingHypotheses.reject: Reject if the signature-only arm can authenticate a token or stage change but cannot map it to one trigger ordinal.

competingHypotheses.claim: Clock identity is counter-equivalent only under a non-overlapping declared uncertainty envelope.
competingHypotheses.prediction: Tight ±40-microsecond intervals remain within one trigger decision cell; loose ±60-microsecond intervals cross a boundary and must be reported ambiguous even when timestamp centers are regular.
competingHypotheses.decisiveTest: The same structural trials adjudicated under both frozen envelopes.
competingHypotheses.reject: Reject if the loose arm asserts robust exact identity or the tight arm cannot map a non-reset event uniquely.

expectedAdjudication.observableExact: counter-plus-Merkle must name both injected stage and trigger ordinal for omission, duplicate, and adjacent reorder at all stages and payload mutation at export or package: 55 trials.
expectedAdjudication.reset: counter-plus-Merkle must name the first affected stage and position but refuse all downstream physical identity until an authenticated new-domain bridge is supplied: 15 trials.
expectedAdjudication.precommit: capture payload mutation must be marked outside-observable-boundary, not clean and not exact-localized: 5 trials.
expectedAdjudication.baselines: Baseline arms are scored for event identity, stage attribution, payload integrity, and refusal separately; partial evidence is not promoted to exact event-and-stage localization.

hardGates: The five placements, three stages, five fault transformations, four arms, two clock envelopes, and expected H1 counts are immutable after this precommit.
The primary Node implementation must verify every generated Ed25519 boundary signature and recompute every Merkle root before scoring a trial.
The Python implementation regenerates corpus bytes, faults, roots, signatures, and verdicts from this precommit and fixed seed without reading the Node result file.
Exact localization requires both the physical trigger ordinal and the first fault boundary. An anonymous token or final-sequence position is not a physical identity.
A reset without a new signed domain identifier and bridge must be refused, even if a heuristic continuation appears unique.
Capture payload mutation is outside the first commitment's observable boundary and must never be counted as detected.
All five clean controls must remain clean; one false localization rejects H1.
Any primary/independent mismatch stops integration and preserves both outputs.
causalChain: Complete synthetic trigger roster, fixed event domain, deterministic bytes, and stage ordering
loss of physical identity when records are removed, copied, reordered, reset, or altered across pipeline boundaries
counter binds records to triggers while a signed boundary root binds ordered identities to payload digests and predecessor state
independent event mapping, root/signature verification, first-differing-boundary detection, and explicit abstention/refusal classify each trial
zero clean false calls plus exact localization of every observable fault establishes the prospective identity-plane criterion; pre-commit and reset limits remain stated rather than erased
fastFailureTests: Stop on the first non-deterministic corpus digest, malformed uint encoding, invalid signature, or Merkle disagreement.
Reject a baseline exact claim if it names only a record position, token digest, or nearest timestamp without a unique physical trigger and stage.
Stop if the loose-clock interval is silently replaced with a point estimate or if reset records reuse the old domain as accepted identities.
Stop if the independent implementation reads the Node outcome file or imports Node-generated trial verdicts.

uncertaintyBudget.measurement: Synthetic timestamps and trigger counts are exact by construction; real oscillators add synchronization, latency, drift, quantization, wrap, and missed-trigger uncertainty not estimated here.
uncertaintyBudget.model: The experiment assumes one trigger produces at most one record, only one injected fault per trial, and no legitimate reordering or many-to-one integration window.
uncertaintyBudget.cryptographic: SHA-256 and Ed25519 are exercised for implementation correctness, not cryptanalytic strength. The published demo private key supplies no operational authenticity.
uncertaintyBudget.implementation: Node and Python share the written specification and fixed test seed, so agreement detects independent coding divergence but not a mistaken common scientific model.
uncertaintyBudget.sampling: Five fixed placements exercise early, interior, power-of-two-adjacent, middle, and late positions; they do not estimate a stochastic field failure rate.
uncertaintyBudget.externalValidity: No conclusion about the unavailable X16 FPGA index, the completeness of XYPT, or a production fab identity plane follows from synthetic success.
uncertaintyBudget.extrapolation: Transfer to asynchronous multi-sensor process windows requires a new many-to-many lineage model and is outside RC49.

safetyEthicsEnvironment: Synthetic 32-byte records only; no personal data, malware, device actuation, production credentials, hazardous procedure, or manufacturing certification. The fixed test key must never be reused operationally.
minimumAdvance: A negative universal result is still useful: it identifies the first commitment as an information boundary and converts vague provenance language into a fault-by-fault matrix of exact identity, stage attribution, integrity, ambiguity, and mandatory refusal.
